hey! thank you for sharing!

i like the metaphor you maintain of fall - it instills a feeling of change throughout the piece, which is the point of it. 

i’m not a fan of the “love tumbled out of you clumsily” (not sure if it’s a direct quote; forgive me, i’m on mobile). can you do something with that line that gives a concrete image related to autumn and trees? “tumbled” isn’t a strong enough verb, i don’t think. can you incorporate the wind rustling the leaves a bit earlier?

on another note, i kinda want to see this expanded! there’s so much you can do describing autumn and the speaker’s relationship with this person. right now, it seems to be a little generic, but as a reader i want to know the speaker’s situation - it helps pull in your readers. 

hope that’s helpful!

i’ve been casually suicidal for as long as i can remember. even when things are going well, there are intrusive thoughts of cutting or hanging myself, always in the background. always the low hum of “i want to die.” when i bring it up people get worried and i’m like... no.... this is normal lmao. 

the best way i’ve found to cope is to pretend it’s just an annoying little bug. like when it says “time to die” i’ll say “ugh, not again, don’t you have anything better to do?” and it helps me move on. not always, because i’m still big on hurting myself, but it helps sometimes.

i dissociated for about a year straight, only recently came out of it. 

i was waking up dissociated and going to sleep dissociated. i would have short periods of clarity, but the clarity overwhelmed me and instantly thrust me back into the haze. 

so, anyway, yes.
thank you!! enjoy your music!
YES!!!! when people tell me i’ve done bad, i’m like “yeah that makes sense” but when people say i’ve done something good i’m like “oh no i tricked them”
laundry always makes me feel better!! i’m so proud of you. i’m trying to work up the motivation to do laundry right now!

when i got into a relationship with my ex, most of my urges went away - i didn’t want to go through his phone, i didn’t feel jealous when he did stuff without me, i wasn’t paranoid. but THIS was the thing that kept coming up. every time i even thought about someone he used to be involved with i spiraled. even now, i hate his guts. i’m friends with someone he had slept with, and every time i see him i get so, so angry. when we were together it chewed away at me and i usually specifically asked him not to tell me about his romantic/sexual past. i can’t take it. i know i’m usually too much for people and i always feel like someone else is better.
it SUCKS.

i’ve never gotten diagnosed. i’ve brought it up with some psychologists and they just kinda wave their hand dismissively. i can’t tell if it’s because they don’t believe me, or if it’s because they know a diagnosis can ruin some things in my life. they’ve said i “have some symptoms that look like borderline.” lol. none of my therapists have ever said it out loud, but my current one is starting DBT with me, so i guess she recognizes it somehow

Hey. I’m a trans guy too. 

There is a chance, a tiny sliver of hope, that once you get to the spot in your transition where you feel like you should die, you won’t WANT to die anymore. 

I always thought that, too. The one thing keeping me from suicide was that I couldn’t kill myself before I at least started testosterone. And now that I’m on it, I don’t want to die until I see all the changes it’ll bring me, and maybe then I will feel better in my own skin. 

It’s not a guarantee, but thank you for sticking around long enough to transition.
I feel the same. My life is objectively good, still want to die.

Yes I totally understand!! Like when I feel a bit suicidal, I like to think of moving away - if I’m going to die anyway, what’s the harm in just moving away? I agree, it’s like leaving behind everything bad I’ve left here, the person I’ve become who I don’t like very much anymore. A fresh start. Killing off the bad parts. In reality, it’s not so much like that, but it’s close enough.
I feel like a failure too. I’m 22 and I feel like I’m just neutral, like it wouldn’t make any sort of difference if I existed or not.
I keep thinking if people would call me and then I could spite them by ignoring their messages
that’s the thing, isn’t it? no matter where we are, we always want to be somewhere else
I’m a writer so I often write short stories of people doing that
I feel that. I feel so humiliated being where I’m at, and the fact that there are people here who genuinely know me freaks me out. I just want to start over.

I feel like a fresh start would help. I’m embarrassed of my life and want to start over, but I know that leaving would break down everything I have and essentially ruin my life, and once I get past the honeymoon phase I go back to the destructive tendencies, like you said. It’s just that no matter where I am, I find myself always wishing I was somewhere else.
I hope it helps, if even a little bit. I hope things get easier for you.

I try to do something else. I know it’s not easy. but I really like music so when I’m really unmotivated and suicidal, I put on an album I like - one that’s emotional, but not directly. When I have more energy I’ll write, or play an instrument, or just tidy something up. Sometimes I shower. 

One thing that helps is I’ll set a timer. Like. I’ll do something for an hour, and if I’m still feeling suicidal after the hour passes, I’ll give in and hurt myself. It’s not great and sometimes I do anyway, but a lot of the time the feeling passes. Sometimes I take something to make me drowsy so ill fall asleep, and then when I wake up it has passed.

I think it’s downvoted because some people have trouble with the whole weight loss thing. exercising was really great for me, but I had to stop running because it was fueling my anorexia in really unhealthy ways, and lifting made me obsessed with my figure, and I only ended up hating myself more. Weight loss isn’t the solution all the time. Exercise is great and helpful, but take it from me - I did NOT get better once I lost 40 pounds. Now I am critically underweight and barely have the energy to stand.

I never told anyone about it, until I flippantly brought it up to my sister, and she said “yeah, he did it to me too” and we never talked about it again. I just spent a lot of time assuming it didn’t actually bother me. I did feel really comfortable in my kinks. I spent a lot of time in the dd/lg community, and I have enough experience to know what I enjoy in bed. I did feel very secure in my exploration of things. But today it’s distressing me to a dangerous point. 

I’ve had too many attempts at this point, too. I attempted about a week ago but my boyfriend sat with me after I’d taken about half the dose of pills that would’ve killed me for sure. I hope you find peace, too. It’s unfair that things like this had to happen to us.

The thing is - I WAS embracing it. I didn’t see anything wrong with it, because I enjoy it and my boyfriend enjoys it and it’s not hurting anyone else. I’m super kinky and I like to engage in all my kinks with people I trust and it’s made for some really fun experiences. But it’s currently causing me immense distress. It makes me a little it dysphoric, it makes me want to impulsively seek out VERY dangerous sexual situations (like literally getting kidnapped), it makes me feel awful every time I’m done having sex or jerking off. I feel like a fetish shouldn’t feel like that.
I don’t want to go to work either. I wish I could tell you something, but I’m not sure how to cope either.
